name: Peter
description: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament

points: He saw two fishermen, Peter and Andrew, and said follow me and I will make you fishers of men. He saw something in two men and brought them into the ministry. Nobody comes in with everything together; our job is to restore you as a man and a god on the earth.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

points: The first thing wives say about submission is, as unto the Lord, and you are not Christ; Jesus would not say what you are saying. Really? Peter took him and began to rebuke him, and he turned and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan. Peter was called Satan himself. What is worse than being called Satan? Nobody wants to admit to being rightfully called something. Not that we should be calling each other out of our names, but there are times you need to realize what spirit you are carrying, and that is what Christ did: I see the spirit on you and I am going to tell you what it is.

note.label: Agree Together | Bound Not Bondage

points: Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee. Peter looked at Christ's death as a bad thing.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

points: But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan. What happened there? Satan literally jumped on Peter. That was not Peter; that was Satan talking to Christ through Peter, and Christ was literally talking to Satan. That is why in another place Christ told Peter, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

points: Now the true flip side. Peter asked, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance; Christ's seventy times seven is complete, boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to extend the same.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Peter asks how often he must forgive, till seven times, and is answered, until seventy times seven.

note.label: Matthew 18: Offences, the Rule for a Trespassing Brother, and Forgiveness

points: Then answered Peter and said unto him, Behold, we have forsaken all, and followed thee. Peter forsook everything to follow Christ. My question to you: do you have that state of mind, that you are willing to forsake everything to follow after Christ? Kanye was not willing to do that. Nick Cannon was not willing to do that; they would lose billions of dollars. Are you willing to lose everything to follow after Christ? That is what this truth is about.

note.label: God, Purpose, and Sacrifice

points: Whom say ye that I am? Peter answers, Thou art the Christ.

note.label: Mark 8: The Four Thousand, the Confession of Peter, and the Cross

points: Peter takes him and begins to rebuke him, and is answered, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.

note.label: Mark 8: The Four Thousand, the Confession of Peter, and the Cross

points: He is transfigured before Peter, James and John, and there appear unto them Elias with Moses, talking with him.

note.label: Mark 9: The Transfiguration, the Dumb Spirit, and Who Shall Be Greatest

points: Peter offers to build three tabernacles, not knowing what to say, for they were sore afraid.

note.label: Mark 9: The Transfiguration, the Dumb Spirit, and Who Shall Be Greatest

points: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled? Their question was: when will this temple be destroyed, when shall the end come?

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: He teaches the people out of Simon's ship, then tells him to launch out into the deep and let down the nets for a draught.

note.label: Luke 5: The Draught of Fishes and the Calling of Sinners

points: Peter falls down at his knees saying, Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.

note.label: Luke 5: The Draught of Fishes and the Calling of Sinners

points: Whom say ye that I am? Peter answering said, The Christ of God.

note.label: Luke 9: The Twelve Sent, the Confession, and the Cost of Following

points: Peter and John are sent to prepare the passover. Christ kept the passover, and a follower of Christ keeps what he kept.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

points: Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat. A lot of you, when you step into that position as a judge, you forgot this scripture right here.

note.label: Called to Judge: Commanded to Be Just

points: Simon, Simon, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: he desires every one of us in here who calls himself repentant.

note.label: Mind Control & The Power Of Prayer

points: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat. So we can all put ourselves in Peter's shoes right here. The Lord said, listen, Satan wants to take all of us out and sift us as wheat.

note.label: Ignite Your Influence

points: Peter denies him three times, and the third time he is known by his speech, for he is a Galilaean. He sounded like the man he was denying.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

points: The Lord turned, and looked upon Peter; and Peter remembered the word of the Lord, and went out, and wept bitterly.

note.label: Luke 22: The Passover, the Betrayal, and the Denial

points: Their words seemed to them as idle tales, and they believed them not. Peter ran to the sepulchre, saw the linen clothes laid by themselves, and departed wondering.

note.label: Luke 24: The Resurrection and the Opening of the Scriptures

points: Andrew first findeth his own brother Simon, and saith unto him, We have found the Messias, and brought him to Jesus, who said, Thou shalt be called Cephas.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

points: Peter cut the man's ear off trying a heroic act, and he was trying to stop the mission from going on. The cup had to be drunk; that good deed turned out a bad result.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs. If you love me, feed my lambs.

note.label: Give Diligence

points: He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

note.label: Give Diligence

points: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep. Do not forget, you were chosen to feed my sheep. You made this agreement, this covenant with me in the heavens before you came to the earth. Do not forget to feed my sheep. His commander gave him his orders and made sure he did not forget them. He repeated them three times before he left him.

note.label: Give Diligence

points: The lists differ across the gospels. Simon is also called Peter and Cephas. Simon the Canaanite is the same as Simon Zelotes. Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus, is the same as Judas the brother of James, who is also called Jude.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

points: Hearing this they were pricked in their heart and asked what they should do, because Peter convinced them by prophecy that this was the man David and the prophets spoke of. The difference between then and now is that they knew their nationality but not Christ; today people accept Christ worldwide, so our ministry expounds that Christ was black and that salvation is to Israel.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

points: Peter and John go up to the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour. Counting the way the scripture counts, the day starts at six in the morning: six is the start, so the third hour is nine in the morning, the sixth hour is noon, and the ninth hour is three in the afternoon. Write that down, because knowing how the hours are counted keeps you from being confused later.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: Peter says, "Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk." This is why, when people at camp ask if we give money to the poor, we say no. A lot of times we do not know why the Most High put a person in that condition, and the money could end up feeding a drug dealer, a drug addict, or a child molester without our knowing it.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: All the people see him walking and praising the Most High, know he is the one who sat for alms at the Beautiful gate, and are filled with wonder, running together to Peter and John at the porch called Solomon's. Notice it says "all the people," because a book establishes its characters at the start and then speaks in pronouns, "he," "she," "they," "all," without re-naming the people every time.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: When Peter sees it he answers, "Ye men of Israel, why marvel ye at this? or why look ye so earnestly on us, as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?" This is the verse that establishes the audience: the "all the people" of verse 11 are the men of Israel.

The healing was not by Peter's own power or holiness. He was not God for doing the work, any more than Elijah was God for raising the dead; it was done by the power of the Most High. This is why the book of Acts is so important, because if you get well versed in Acts you can spiritually kill the white supremacist doctrine and the wicked Christian mindset that has been planted in our people's minds.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: When they had set them in the midst, they asked by what power or by what name have ye done this, and Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, ye rulers of the people and elders of Israel. The conversation is still to Israel, always the Israelites. Being filled with the Holy Ghost did not mean Peter was shaking, sweating, or speaking in tongues; it means he was filled with the wisdom to speak with poise before the rulers.

Peter, Paul, John, and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque, or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged, and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

points: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John. They saw the boldness of Peter. And John. So Peter was not the only one rolling like Christ. Peter and John.

note.label: I Need More Confidence

points: When they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled and took knowledge of them that they had been with Jesus. The rulers saw these men were not slick, cunning, and crafty like themselves; they were bold, coming as if straight off a plantation and a field, not the regular church men. That boldness is the natural animation of the Holy Spirit, not something you force or make up.

Peter was fearless and intrepid, a man who drew a sword and cut off the man's ear, which was not the first time he used it; he came from the streets, and we have brothers with that same posture. They took knowledge the disciples had been with Christ because you take on the attributes and characteristics of whoever you surround yourself with, and the disciples all spoke the same thing as Christ.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

points: But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost? The war always starts in the mind, and Satan is the one who puts these things there. The thought came into his mind: you do not have to tell the apostles how much you really sold the land for. He could have said, no, I cannot think like that; but he gave in to the thought, and then he went and lied to the apostles. That is how Satan attacks: he whispers things in your mind, and if you are not careful and vigilant and paying attention to your thoughts, you will defile yourself and get caught up in sin.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness Part 2

points: But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost? That is what happened with Cain, and that is what Satan does to us: he fills the heart.

Ananias and Sapphira sold their possession, and Satan came to them and said, act like you are giving them all the money, but keep back part for yourself, and do not let them know anything. If they wanted to keep back part for themselves, they could have just told Peter openly: we kept back a little part, and this part we are giving to the church. But Satan told them to hide it. The reason that thought came to their mind was Satan.

note.label: Leaven: The Root of Bitterness

points: Why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost? The devil convinced them nobody would know, because they did not look at Peter as a spiritual man, the same way some of you sit at this table and lie to the leaders' faces.

note.label: Dark Places of the Heart: the Hidden Cost of Sin

points: Peter asks why Satan has filled Ananias' heart to lie to the Holy Ghost and keep back part of the price; while it remained it was his own, so he has not lied unto men but unto the Most High.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

points: By the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were wrought; they were together in Solomon's porch, believers were the more added, and multitudes brought the sick into the streets on beds and couches that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow them, and they were healed every one.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

points: When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of the Most High, they sent Peter and John, who prayed for them that they might receive the Holy Ghost. Notice the order: Philip, the deacon, woke up the city and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them. It is the same order today, where the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: But Peter said, Thy money perish with thee: that was covetousness and envy. I want to do what they are doing; that spirit ferments bitterness. You think because you have money and connections you are supposed to have an office, and that you are above correction. No: the Lord is the one raising up the men.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

points: Peter said, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of the Most High may be purchased with money; thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter, for thy heart is not right. Repent therefore of this thy wickedness and pray, for I perceive thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: As Peter passes through all quarters he comes to the saints at Lydda and finds Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years sick of the palsy. Peter says, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole; arise and make thy bed," and he arises immediately.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

points: The disciples send for Peter, who puts them all out, kneels, prays, and says, "Tabitha, arise." She opens her eyes and sits up, and he presents her alive to the saints and widows, so that many in Joppa believed. Peter then tarries many days in Joppa with Simon a tanner.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

points: Peter went up upon the housetop to pray about the sixth hour: this is the noonday prayer. Remember in Psalms 55:17 it says pray three times, evening, morning, and noon.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: On the next day, as the men drew near the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray about the sixth hour. He became very hungry, and while they made ready he fell into a trance.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Rise, Peter: it is time to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. Kill: kill the old man, mortify yourself, discipline yourself. Eat: devour wisdom, learn the scripture. And then go out and teach. But in that time there was no New Testament: Peter would have to explain it to those of the circumcision using the Old Testament.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: And the voice spake unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, that call not thou common. The subject matter of the cleansing is man; and to explain that cleansing, Peter would have to use the Old Testament.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: A voice said, "Rise, Peter; kill, and eat," but Peter answered, "Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean." Peter refuses because he knows the dietary law, that there is a beast that may be eaten and a beast that may not.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: The vision was not really talking about food. That is why it says Peter doubted in himself what this vision should mean: is the Lord telling me to eat unlawful animals? When visions come from God, they are an allegory, referring to something else.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: This was done thrice, and the vessel was received up again into heaven. While Peter doubted in himself what the vision meant, the men sent from Cornelius had already found Simon's house and stood before the gate, asking whether Simon called Peter lodged there.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: Write this down: Caesarea is in the land of Israel; it is in the land of West Manasseh, right beside Samaria. Map shown on screen. Deacon: Peter lived in Joppa, the seaport there; he sailed up north to visit Cornelius. Christ was raised further up, Galilee, so he was raised around them in that area. And that place Scythopolis means city of the Scythians; Scythians is northern kingdom also. That's who Paul wrote to in Colossians 3:11.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: As Peter came in, Cornelius fell down at his feet and worshipped him. But Peter took him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons. Now this is where Christians get you: they'll read verse 34 and 35. But the next verse explains Cornelius: the word which God sent unto the children of Israel. So Acts 10 is telling you that this was for the children of Israel. But because of supersessionism, replacement theology, we go, oh, God accepts everybody; this Cornelius was a white man, an Italian man, a Roman. That's replacement theology.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons. Northern kingdom, southern kingdom: he is no respecter of persons.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: While Peter yet spake, the Holy Ghost fell on all who heard, and they of the circumcision were astonished that on the "Gentiles" also the gift was poured out, for they spake with tongues and magnified the Most High. The Spirit is poured only on the house of Israel, so the Gentiles receiving it are the children of Israel, the northern kingdom.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

points: When Peter came up to Jerusalem, they of the circumcision contended with him, saying he went in to men uncircumcised and did eat with them. The complaint was about Peter dealing with the Gentiles, meaning the northern kingdom, and there had been contention between the northern and southern kingdom ever since the split under Solomon.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

points: Peter continues the account: immediately three men came to the house from Caesarea, and the Spirit bade him go with them, nothing doubting. Six brethren went with him into the man's house, and Cornelius told how an angel had stood in his house and directed him to send to Joppa for Simon Peter, who would tell him words whereby he and all his house would be saved.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

points: After three years of teaching, Paul went up to Jerusalem to see Peter and stayed with him fifteen days. The apostles were not aware of what Paul had been doing; he was doing these things having not been taught by Peter and the others.

note.label: Galatians 1: Paul's Apostleship and the True Gospel

points: In Acts 11:2-3, those of the circumcision contended with Peter for going to men uncircumcised. Romans 3:1 shows the Jews were called the circumcision because they kept the covenant of circumcision established to Abraham.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Paul's ministry was given to him by Christ and was directed to the uncircumcision, just as Peter's ministry was to the circumcision, also wrought by Christ. The uncircumcision was also called the Gentiles; these terms mean one and the same.
In Acts 11:1, the apostles heard that the Gentiles had received the word of God, referring specifically to Cornelius. In Acts 10:31-36, Peter explains his encounter with Cornelius.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: James, Cephas, and John gave Paul and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision. The heathen: talking about the northern kingdom.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: They saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter, for he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles. Christ worked in Peter toward the Jews born and raised in the law and circumcised the eighth day, and the same Christ worked in Paul toward the dispersed. James, Cephas, and John gave the right hands of fellowship that we should go unto the heathen and they unto the circumcision, remembering the poor.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: This history is not recorded in Acts. After Paul was in Antioch doing his ministry, Peter came along later.
Paul confronted Peter to his face because he was at fault. Peter, being the head apostle and second in command from Christ, still made mistakes.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? Peter knew better. He was corrected in front of them all, and he would have been embarrassed and ashamed. But he repented; and as a teacher, what do you teach after that? What you repented from: do not be fake.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

points: When Peter was come to Antioch, in Turkey like Galatia, I withstood him to the face. He ate with the Gentiles, but when certain came from James he withdrew, fearing them of the circumcision, and the other Jews and even Barnabas dissembled with him. If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of the Gentiles, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews? You cannot teach the scattered sinners of the Gentiles who they are and then act like you are not with them; that is a bad example.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: Paul confronted Peter in front of everybody. He said: you claim to be a Jew, salvation is of the Jews, and you are supposed to be an example, but you are doing the same thing the northern kingdom was doing.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

points: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia.

note.label: The Slave Mentality Yesterday & Today: the True Diaspora

points: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. So he is not just dealing with Ephesus, Peter is also dealing with other places where the Israelites are scattered.

And Peter's epistles come after his growth, after learning so much and making so many mistakes. When we read Galatians 2, and when we read in John where Christ said Satan desires to have you and sift you as wheat, Peter's epistles are after all that. Satan desires to have you. Brothers, Satan desires to have you. Young men, Satan desires to have you. Sisters, Satan desires to have you. Just like Peter. Peter's epistles come after he finally realised the cock had crowed thrice and Christ looked at him and he wept sore. All of these things are now a part of his understanding, where he can write his epistle with much more clarity than when he was actually walking with Christ.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

points: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia, elect according to the foreknowledge of God. Isaiah 45:4 says 'Israel mine elect.' The strangers are Israelites.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers
